Chapter 10: Sustaining Simplicity Through Life’s Changes
You know, life never really stands still. Our homes, just like us, are always evolving—sometimes slowly, sometimes all at once. Maybe you’re moving to a new place, welcoming a new family member, or suddenly working from home. These big changes can shake up even the most carefully organized spaces, and all of a sudden, clutter starts creeping back in.
So, how do you keep things simple when everything around you is shifting? The secret is to treat decluttering as an ongoing practice, not just a one-off project. Think of your home like a garden. It doesn’t matter how beautifully you planted it last spring—you still need to check in, pull a few weeds, and make adjustments as the seasons change.
Here are a few ways you can do that:
First, try scheduling seasonal refreshes. Every few months, take a little time to look around and see what still fits your life and what’s just taking up space. Letting go can feel surprisingly freeing.
Next, set up storage that’s flexible. Maybe that means baskets that move from room to room, or shelves that can be rearranged as your needs shift. The goal is to make it easy to adapt as life changes.
And most importantly, be gentle with yourself—especially during times of upheaval. Order in your home will ebb and flow, and that’s completely normal. Give yourself the grace to adjust and find your rhythm again.
It also helps to plan ahead for those big transitions. For example, if you’re about to move, carve out some time to sort through your things before you start packing. That way, you’ll only bring along what truly matters. If you’re welcoming a new child or even a new pet, try carving out dedicated spaces for their things, and tweak your routines so everyone feels at home.
In the end, the best thing you can do is greet change with curiosity and openness. Every new chapter in life gives you a chance to realign your home with what matters most to you right now—not just what made sense last year.
So, stay tuned in to what feels supportive and let go of what doesn’t. That’s how you’ll keep that wonderful sense of clarity and ease, no matter how much life throws your way.
